title: The cross-environment measurement, and the instruments that make it readable
note: R59 spent weeks on a number that was a slice width, resting on a comparison that could not have disagreed with itself, with a fingerprint naming the build kernel rather than the running one. E1-E2 attack the fingerprint field the whole attribution turns on. E3-E7 attack the sensitivity sweep, including the two ways it can vary nothing and still report a result, and the numpy row without which the attribution stops at 'the counts are close'. E8-E11 attack the container script's step record and its ordering -- the record exists because 'steps 1-3 passed' was an inference from set -e ordering, and the ordering matters because set -e once skipped the diagnostic in exactly the case it was written for. E18-E20 attack the second empty comparison: two byte-identical trees, which is not an error and must not be refused, but which printed the measurement's headline after classifying nothing (D-2026-62). X1-X28 (D-2026-100) replace E12-E20: the comparator rewritten -- exact scope, structural and decision refusal, integers and exact columns discrete, NaN/Inf refused, unparsed artefacts unclassified, zero crossings and sign flips permitted only under a quantity-bound BELOW_RESOLUTION class inside its floor, scientific equivalence never claimed.

mutations.name: E1_the_fingerprint_names_the_build_kernel_again
mutations.rationale: the field the whole cross-environment comparison turns on goes back to being absent, so a divergence has no kernel beside it and the build string -- which says Haswell on a machine that selects SkylakeX -- is the only thing left to read

mutations.name: E2_the_runtime_core_lookup_gives_up_silently
mutations.rationale: the library exports the symbol and this stops looking for it, so every fingerprint records UNKNOWN and the attribution rests on nothing

mutations.name: E3_a_kernel_the_host_cannot_run_is_a_failed_measurement
mutations.find: measured = [r for r in runs if not r.get("unsupported")]
mutations.rationale: 'the tool broke' and 'this CPU cannot execute the kernel the committed outputs were produced with' become the same verdict -- and the second one is the single most useful row a hosted runner produces

mutations.name: E4_a_sweep_that_varied_nothing_is_accepted
mutations.rationale: every row falling back to one kernel reports 'no difference anywhere' -- a true sentence about a comparison that varied no variable

mutations.name: E5_a_sweep_of_one_row_reports_a_dependence
mutations.rationale: a single measured row is enough to publish a sensitivity result, which is a claim about a comparison that never happened

mutations.name: E6_numpys_own_dispatch_is_never_pinned
mutations.find:
if npy_disable is not None:
        env["NPY_DISABLE_CPU_FEATURES"] = npy_disable
mutations.rationale: the row that reproduces a host without AVX-512 stops pinning the thing that made it reproduce -- and the attribution falls back to 'the counts are close', which is where the investigation was stuck

mutations.name: E7_an_inherited_pin_is_carried_into_every_row
mutations.rationale: a sweep run in an already-pinned shell reports the shell's dispatch under every row's name, so the rows agree and nothing is measured

mutations.name: E8_the_container_forgets_how_far_it_got
mutations.rationale: the step record goes back to being readable only by scrolling to a part of the log the API does not serve, which is what made 'steps 1-3 passed' an inference

mutations.name: E9_a_completed_step_is_not_recorded
mutations.rationale: the summary prints an empty list however far the run got, so the record says nothing and looks like it says something

mutations.name: E10_the_failing_step_is_not_named
mutations.rationale: a failing run names no failing step, so the summary tells you what worked and not what did not

mutations.name: E11_the_diagnostic_runs_after_the_check_that_fails
mutations.find:
step "cross-environment-3d"
python analysis/collect_container_3d.py /tmp/qta-3d-diag --emit-summary
done_ "cross-environment-3d"

step "package_consistency"
python package_consistency_check.py
done_ "package_consistency"

step "manuscript_consistency"
python manuscript_consistency_check.py
done_ "manuscript_consistency"
mutations.replace:
step "package_consistency"
python package_consistency_check.py
done_ "package_consistency"

step "manuscript_consistency"
python manuscript_consistency_check.py
done_ "manuscript_consistency"

step "cross-environment-3d"
python analysis/collect_container_3d.py /tmp/qta-3d-diag --emit-summary
done_ "cross-environment-3d"
mutations.rationale: a pure REORDER, not a deletion: every step is still there and still announces itself, so only a test that checks the ORDER can see it. set -e then ends the run at the byte divergence and the diagnostic that exists to EXPLAIN a byte divergence never executes -- the one case the measurement matters most is the one it is skipped in
